question: How do tracing, evaluations, and Signals fit together?
answer:
Tracing records what your application did, evaluations score outputs against a repeatable set of examples, and Signals score and tag recorded agent activity in production. The snapshot I searched didn't include one page that explains all three together, so the framing below is my summary of separate pages.

- **Tracing (the data layer):** For multi-turn agents, Weave's trace integrations capture sessions, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls and show them in the **Agents** view. For plain LLM-call code, they capture individual calls and pipeline steps as **Calls** in the **Traces** view [S5].
- **Evaluations (pre-release testing):** An evaluation compares changes against a consistent set of examples so you can catch regressions before they reach users [S4]. Scorers evaluate AI outputs and return metrics, and you pass them to a `weave.Evaluation` in Python [S3].
- **Signals (production monitoring):** In the Agents view, the Signals tab shows tags and ratings for agent conversations. They flag quality and safety problems, such as low-quality responses, user frustration, or NSFW content, and point you to traces that need attention [S1]. A rating is a 0.0–1.0 score and tags are labels, both assigned to matching spans [S6].

**How they fit:** Tracing produces the records. Evaluations and Signals are two ways of scoring behavior, one on a fixed example set and one on live agent activity. Agent Lens is described as using the same trace data as Weave [S1].

**Caveat:** The older Monitors page describes a previous approach to monitoring production traffic and says new implementations should use Signals under Weave for Agents [S7]. Don't mix the two workflows' instructions.

If you tell me whether you're building a multi-turn agent or an LLM pipeline, I can narrow this to the relevant pages.

sources.title: Integrations overview
sources.heading: Integrations overview
sources.text:
# Integrations overview

> Trace agents and LLM applications with Weave's integrations for agent SDKs, harnesses, LLM providers, and orchestration frameworks.

Weave provides two ways to integrate with your AI stack:

* **Trace agents**: for multi-turn agentic applications built with agent SDKs (such as the OpenAI Agents SDK or Google ADK) or run inside agent harnesses (such as Claude Code, Codex, or Pi.dev). These integrations capture sessions, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls, and render them in the Weave **Agents** view.
* **Trace LLM applications**: for code that calls LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, and others) or uses orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, DSPy, and others). These integrations capture individual LLM calls and pipeline steps as Weave **Calls** in the **Traces** view.

If you're not sure which path to take, start with [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md) for new multi-turn agent work, or [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) for existing LLM-call workflows.

# Build an evaluation

> Learn how to build an evaluation pipeline with Weave Models and Evaluations

[Try in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/wandb/examples/blob/main/colabs/weave/tutorial-eval.ipynb)

[GitHub source](https://github.com/wandb/examples/blob/main/colabs/weave/tutorial-eval.ipynb)

This tutorial walks you through building an end-to-end evaluation pipeline in Weave so you can measure and track the quality of an LLM application as you iterate on it. Evaluations help you compare changes against a consistent set of examples and detect regressions before they reach users. This tutorial targets developers who build LLM-powered applications and want a repeatable way to test them.

Weave provides built-in support for tracking evaluations with [`Model`](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/core-types/models) and [`Evaluation`](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/core-types/evaluations) classes. The APIs make minimal assumptions, so they fit a range of use cases.

![Evals hero](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/images-evals-hero.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=fa65ccc8aa05294f37b3eba5e061ac16)

sources.title: Scoring overview
sources.heading: Scoring overview
sources.text:
# Scoring overview

> Evaluate AI outputs and return evaluation metrics with Weave Scorers

In Weave, Scorers evaluate AI outputs and return evaluation metrics. They take the AI's output, analyze it, and return a dictionary of results. Scorers can use your input data as reference if needed and can also output extra information, such as explanations or reasoning from the evaluation.

This guide is for developers who want to measure the quality of their AI system's outputs. It explains how Scorers fit into Weave evaluations, how to build your own Scorers, how to apply Scorers to individual calls, and how to analyze the resulting scores.

**Python**

Pass Scorers to a `weave.Evaluation` object during evaluation. Weave supports two types of Scorers:

1. **Function-based Scorers:** Python functions decorated with `@weave.op`.
2. **Class-based Scorers:** Python classes that inherit from `weave.Scorer` for more complex evaluations.

Scorers must return a dictionary and can return multiple metrics, nested metrics, and non-numeric values such as text returned from an LLM-evaluator about its reasoning.

**TypeScript**

Scorers are special ops that you pass to a `weave.Evaluation` object during evaluation.

sources.text:
# Monitor your agents with signals

> Use Weave signals to score agent turns, apply tags, and surface quality and safety issues in production.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tags/create-tag.md).

In Weave's [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md), the Signals tab shows tags and ratings for your agent's conversations. Signals surface quality and safety issues to flag problems, find patterns, and highlight the traces that need your attention. Use signals to automatically score the quality of your agent's responses, notice when a user is frustrated, or flag NSFW content.

To score turns with an HTTP endpoint that you host instead of an LLM judge, see [Score agent turns with a remote scorer](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/remote-scorer-signals.md).

sources.heading: Key terms
sources.text:
## Key terms

* **Turn**: One back-and-forth exchange between the user and the agent.
* **Rating**: A numeric score between 0.0 and 1.0 assigned to a matching span.
* **Tags**: Labels assigned to matching spans, such as "user-frustration" or "nsfw".

sources.title: Monitor using built-in signals
sources.heading: Monitor using built-in signals
sources.text:
# Monitor using built-in signals

> Weights & Biases provides built-in scoring solutions for agents in production

> [!NOTE]
>
> This page covers a previous approach to monitoring production traffic. For new implementations, use **Signals** under Weave for Agents. See [View agent signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

Standard system metrics like latency, token count, and cost don't fully capture agent behavior. Inspecting individual traces provides deep insight but doesn't scale to the millions of traces generated in a live environment.

Signals provide a high-level monitoring solution to this problem by offering automated, behavioral scoring for agents in production:

* Automated scoring: Every incoming production trace is automatically processed and scored on common quality issues and errors.
* Infrastructure: Processing is powered by CoreWeave compute and CoreWeave GPUs for scalability across millions of traces.

By using signals within production, you can:

* Gain behavioral insight. Move beyond system metrics to understand if your agent is hallucinating, failing to follow conversation patterns, or losing grounding in its evidence.
* Accelerate the research loop. Use the scores and failure analyses generated by signals to identify weaknesses, which you can use to research model improvement, data annotation, or reinforcement learning.

all_read_evidence.text:
# Integrations overview

> Trace agents and LLM applications with Weave's integrations for agent SDKs, harnesses, LLM providers, and orchestration frameworks.

Weave provides two ways to integrate with your AI stack:

* **Trace agents**: for multi-turn agentic applications built with agent SDKs (such as the OpenAI Agents SDK or Google ADK) or run inside agent harnesses (such as Claude Code, Codex, or Pi.dev). These integrations capture sessions, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls, and render them in the Weave **Agents** view.
* **Trace LLM applications**: for code that calls LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, and others) or uses orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, DSPy, and others). These integrations capture individual LLM calls and pipeline steps as Weave **Calls** in the **Traces** view.

If you're not sure which path to take, start with [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md) for new multi-turn agent work, or [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) for existing LLM-call workflows.

> Use Weave signals to score agent turns, apply tags, and surface quality and safety issues in production.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. all_read_evidence.heading: Monitor using built-in signals
all_read_evidence.text:
# Monitor using built-in signals

> Weights & Biases provides built-in scoring solutions for agents in production

> [!NOTE]
>
> This page covers a previous approach to monitoring production traffic. For new implementations, use **Signals** under Weave for Agents. See [View agent signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

Standard system metrics like latency, token count, and cost don't fully capture agent behavior. Inspecting individual traces provides deep insight but doesn't scale to the millions of traces generated in a live environment.

Signals provide a high-level monitoring solution to this problem by offering automated, behavioral scoring for agents in production:

* Automated scoring: Every incoming production trace is automatically processed and scored on common quality issues and errors.
* Infrastructure: Processing is powered by CoreWeave compute and CoreWeave GPUs for scalability across millions of traces.

By using signals within production, you can:

* Gain behavioral insight. Move beyond system metrics to understand if your agent is hallucinating, failing to follow conversation patterns, or losing grounding in its evidence.
* Accelerate the research loop. Use the scores and failure analyses generated by signals to identify weaknesses, which you can use to research model improvement, data annotation, or reinforcement learning.

## Get started

To open the Agents view for your project:

# Scoring overview

> Evaluate AI outputs and return evaluation metrics with Weave Scorers

In Weave, Scorers evaluate AI outputs and return evaluation metrics. They take the AI's output, analyze it, and return a dictionary of results. Scorers can use your input data as reference if needed and can also output extra information, such as explanations or reasoning from the evaluation.

This guide is for developers who want to measure the quality of their AI system's outputs. It explains how Scorers fit into Weave evaluations, how to build your own Scorers, how to apply Scorers to individual calls, and how to analyze the resulting scores.

**Python**

Pass Scorers to a `weave.Evaluation` object during evaluation. Weave supports two types of Scorers:

1. **Function-based Scorers:** Python functions decorated with `@weave.op`.
2. **Class-based Scorers:** Python classes that inherit from `weave.Scorer` for more complex evaluations.

Scorers must return a dictionary and can return multiple metrics, nested metrics, and non-numeric values such as text returned from an LLM-evaluator about its reasoning.

**TypeScript**

Scorers are special ops that you pass to a `weave.Evaluation` object during evaluation.

# Integrations overview

> Trace agents and LLM applications with Weave's integrations for agent SDKs, harnesses, LLM providers, and orchestration frameworks.

Weave provides two ways to integrate with your AI stack:

* **Trace agents**: for multi-turn agentic applications built with agent SDKs (such as the OpenAI Agents SDK or Google ADK) or run inside agent harnesses (such as Claude Code, Codex, or Pi.dev). These integrations capture sessions, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls, and render them in the Weave **Agents** view.
* **Trace LLM applications**: for code that calls LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, and others) or uses orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, DSPy, and others). These integrations capture individual LLM calls and pipeline steps as Weave **Calls** in the **Traces** view.

If you're not sure which path to take, start with [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md) for new multi-turn agent work, or [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) for existing LLM-call workflows.

result.text:
## Key terms

* **Turn**: One back-and-forth exchange between the user and the agent.
* **Rating**: A numeric score between 0.0 and 1.0 assigned to a matching span.
* **Tags**: Labels assigned to matching spans, such as "user-frustration" or "nsfw".
result.page_context:
# Monitor your agents with signals

> Use Weave signals to score agent turns, apply tags, and surface quality and safety issues in production.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tags/create-tag.md).

In Weave's [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md), the Signals tab shows tags and ratings for your agent's conversations. Signals surface quality and safety issues to flag problems, find patterns, and highlight the traces that need your attention. Use signals to automatically score the quality of your agent's responses, notice when a user is frustrated, or flag NSFW content.

To score turns with an HTTP endpoint that you host instead of an LLM judge, see [Score agent turns with a remote scorer](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/remote-scorer-signals.md).

A rating is a 0.0–1.0 score and tags are labels, both assigned to matching spans [S6].

result.heading: Monitor using built-in signals
result.text:
# Monitor using built-in signals

> Weights & Biases provides built-in scoring solutions for agents in production

> [!NOTE]
>
> This page covers a previous approach to monitoring production traffic. For new implementations, use **Signals** under Weave for Agents. See [View agent signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

Standard system metrics like latency, token count, and cost don't fully capture agent behavior. Inspecting individual traces provides deep insight but doesn't scale to the millions of traces generated in a live environment.

Signals provide a high-level monitoring solution to this problem by offering automated, behavioral scoring for agents in production:

* Automated scoring: Every incoming production trace is automatically processed and scored on common quality issues and errors.
* Infrastructure: Processing is powered by CoreWeave compute and CoreWeave GPUs for scalability across millions of traces.

By using signals within production, you can:

* Gain behavioral insight. Move beyond system metrics to understand if your agent is hallucinating, failing to follow conversation patterns, or losing grounding in its evidence.
* Accelerate the research loop. Use the scores and failure analyses generated by signals to identify weaknesses, which you can use to research model improvement, data annotation, or reinforcement learning.
